correctness.rationale: Equation (1) is verified by a direct rank-one inverse identity, with normalization of the centered norm explicit. A missing-edge incidence vector is a Laplacian eigenvector iff the endpoints are false twins; this is equivalent to rank-one negative semidefiniteness of the difference, while nontwins give independent functionals and strict positive/negative vectors. The complete-multipartite equivalence and minimal connected four-agent example are proved. The exact verifier independently checked 772 connected labeled graphs, 3,227 nonedges and the 501/156800 witness increase.

originality.rationale: The closest full-text 2021 result controls only combined polarization-plus-disagreement P+D, and explicitly notes a failed squared-inverse ordering step. The inspected 2018 paper defines centered P and optimizes P+D globally; the 2019 work changes weights under degree constraints. No inspected paper or targeted literature search establishes the false-twin iff, all-edge complete multipartite iff, or four-agent sharp connected threshold. Novelty is provisional under historical coverage limits.

value.rationale: A natural social-network stability question has an exact topology-only answer for every graph size and all innate opinions: complete multipartite structures, not arbitrary connectedness, are universally safe from an increase after an additional tie. The contrast with P+D monotonicity and the minimal connected four-agent witness make a structural result, not just a numerical counterexample. It does not assert empirical impact.
